description: A blood bank medical director must decide whether to establish an emergency blood-product reserve at an affiliated urgent-care clinic and finalize the product mix, storage safeguards, replenishment schedule, and staff-readiness plan.

shared_context.S1: The affiliated Riverside Urgent Care Clinic has requested an emergency blood-product reserve for use before transfer to the main hospital.
shared_context.S2: The reserve would be stored at Riverside and replenished through the hospital blood bank.
shared_context.S3: Dr. Miriam Chen makes the final decision about whether the reserve may go live and what operating requirements accompany it.
shared_context.S4: Riverside currently has no blood products assigned to its inventory.
shared_context.S5: During the standing implementation huddle, Dr. Chen reviews the reserve plan with transfusion medicine, laboratory operations, courier services, and nursing education before finalizing it.

PF1.text: The transfusion service protocol approved for Riverside requires a starting reserve of exactly 4 O-negative red-cell units and 2 O-positive red-cell units; Dr. Alvarez reviewed the signed protocol, but the inventory request has not yet been entered.

PF2.text: Riverside's blood refrigerator was validated for storage at exactly 2-6 degrees Celsius, and the laboratory acceptance record requires a temperature-alarm test to be documented before any units are stocked; Nora has the validation report.

PF3.text: The courier contract provides blood-product replenishment from the main hospital to Riverside every Tuesday and Friday at 10:00, with a same-day replacement commitment for any unit issued before the next scheduled run; Evan confirmed these terms with the courier vendor.

PF4.text: All seven Riverside nurses who may access the reserve must complete blood-product handling competency training by Friday at 15:00 before the reserve can go live; Tasha has the attendance roster and the educator's competency requirement.

acceptance_conditions: The Riverside reserve must be approved.
The reserve must contain exactly 4 O-negative red-cell units and 2 O-positive red-cell units.
Storage must be set to exactly 2-6 degrees Celsius and an alarm test must be required before stocking.
Replenishment must be scheduled for Tuesday and Friday at 10:00, with same-day replacement after an issued unit.
All seven Riverside nurses must complete training by Friday at 15:00.
The signed transfusion protocol must be cited as justification for approval and the product mix.

content_checks.C3: decisions['storage_temperature_range'] == '2-6 degrees Celsius' or decisions['storage_temperature_range'] == '2-6 C'
content_checks.C7: any((c.get('type') == 'nursing_competency' or c.get('type') == 'nursing_competency_training') and (c.get('target') == 'Tasha Williams' or c.get('target') == 'Nursing Education' or c.get('target') == 'Riverside nurses') and 'seven' in c.get('detail') and 'Friday' in c.get('detail') and '15:00' in c.get('detail') for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The signed protocol changes the decision from an unsupported reserve to approval and fixes the product mix at exactly 4 O-negative and 2 O-positive red-cell units.
The validation report changes storage from an unspecified condition to exactly 2-6 degrees Celsius and requires the alarm-test decision to be true before stocking.
The courier terms change replenishment from an unspecified delivery plan to Tuesday and Friday at 10:00 with same-day replacement after an issued unit.

The competency requirement changes staff readiness from an unspecified training plan to training for exactly seven nurses by Friday at 15:00 and requires a corresponding nursing competency commitment.
